records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — [confidence 75][P2] `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` invokes a String method on an untyped required parameter, so an authenticated request with `usernames[]=alice` passes parameter presence validation and raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation response.
records.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug in the diff. Looking at line 71 in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb: `usernames.split(",").each do |username|`. The parameter is obtained via `params.require(:usernames)` which ensures presence but not type. If a client sends `usernames[]=alice` (array format), Rails will pass an Array object, and calling `.split(",")` on an Array will raise NoMethodError since Array doesn't have a split method. This is a valid input validation bug that could cause a 500 error instead of a proper validation response.
